title: Who founded the Maratha Empire?
description: Who is regarded as the founder of the Maratha Empire?
hint: He established an independent Maratha kingdom in western India.
summary: Shivaji Maharaj is regarded as the founder of the Maratha Empire.

title: Where was Shivaji Maharaj born?
description: Identify the birthplace of Shivaji Maharaj.
hint: The fort is located in present-day Pune district.
summary: Shivaji Maharaj was born at Shivneri Fort.

title: Who was Shivaji's mother?
description: Who was the mother of Shivaji Maharaj?
hint: She was the wife of Shahaji Bhonsle.
summary: Jijabai was the mother of Shivaji Maharaj.

title: Who was Shivaji's father?
description: Identify the father of Shivaji Maharaj.
hint: He served various Deccan powers, including the Ahmadnagar and Bijapur states.
summary: Shahaji Bhonsle was the father of Shivaji Maharaj.

title: Which fort did Shivaji capture in 1646?
description: Which fort was captured by Shivaji in 1646, marking an early step in his territorial expansion?
hint: The fort was earlier known as Murumbdev.
summary: Shivaji captured Torna Fort in 1646.

title: Which fort became the capital of Shivaji's kingdom?
description: Which fort served as the principal capital of Shivaji Maharaj's kingdom?
hint: It was formerly known as Rairi.
summary: Raigad Fort became the capital of Shivaji's kingdom.

title: When was Shivaji crowned?
description: In which year was Shivaji Maharaj formally crowned at Raigad?
hint: The coronation took place in the 17th century.
summary: Shivaji Maharaj was crowned in 1674.

title: Who performed Shivaji's coronation ceremony?
description: Who presided over Shivaji's coronation ceremony at Raigad?
hint: He was a renowned Brahmin scholar from Varanasi.
summary: Gaga Bhatt performed Shivaji's coronation ceremony.

title: Which title did Shivaji assume at his coronation?
description: What royal title did Shivaji Maharaj adopt at his coronation?
hint: The title means king or sovereign.
summary: Shivaji assumed the title Chhatrapati.

title: Who was defeated by Shivaji at Pratapgad?
description: Which Bijapur general was defeated and killed during the encounter at Pratapgad?
hint: He was sent by the Adil Shahi ruler of Bijapur.
summary: Afzal Khan was defeated and killed during the Pratapgad encounter in 1659.

title: Who led the Mughal campaign against Shivaji in 1665?
description: Which Mughal general negotiated the Treaty of Purandar with Shivaji?
hint: He was a Rajput ruler from Amber.
summary: Raja Jai Singh I led the Mughal campaign against Shivaji in 1665.

title: What was the Treaty of Purandar signed in?
description: In which year was the Treaty of Purandar signed between Shivaji and the Mughals?
hint: It followed Jai Singh's campaign against Shivaji.
summary: The Treaty of Purandar was signed in 1665.

title: Where was Shivaji detained by Aurangzeb?
description: In which city was Shivaji placed under detention after visiting Aurangzeb's court?
hint: The city was the Mughal imperial capital at the time.
summary: Shivaji was detained at Agra in 1666.

title: Who escaped from Agra with Shivaji?
description: Who accompanied Shivaji during his escape from Mughal detention at Agra?
hint: He was Shivaji's son and later succeeded him.
summary: Sambhaji accompanied Shivaji during the escape from Agra.

title: Which fort was renamed Raigad?
description: Which fort, originally known as Rairi, was developed and renamed Raigad by Shivaji?
hint: It became the capital of Shivaji's kingdom.
summary: Rairi Fort was renamed Raigad.

title: Who was Tanaji Malusare?
description: Tanaji Malusare was a prominent commander associated with which Maratha ruler?
hint: He fought in the campaign to recapture Kondhana.
summary: Tanaji Malusare was a prominent commander of Shivaji Maharaj.

title: What was Kondhana later called?
description: The fort of Kondhana was renamed by Shivaji in memory of Tanaji Malusare.
hint: It is located near Pune.
summary: Kondhana was renamed Sinhagad after Tanaji's death.

title: What was Shivaji's naval force called?
description: Which branch of Shivaji's military was developed to protect the western coastline?
hint: It consisted of ships and sailors.
summary: Shivaji developed a naval force to protect the Konkan coast.

title: Which fort was a major naval base of Shivaji?
description: Which sea fort in the Konkan region became an important naval base under Shivaji?
hint: It is located off the Malvan coast.
summary: Sindhudurg was an important naval fort of Shivaji.

title: What was the Ashta Pradhan?
description: What did the Ashta Pradhan refer to in Shivaji's administration?
hint: The name literally refers to eight principal ministers.
summary: Ashta Pradhan was a council of eight ministers under Shivaji.

title: Who was the first Peshwa under Shivaji?
description: Who held the office of Peshwa in Shivaji's Ashta Pradhan council?
hint: He was one of Shivaji's principal ministers.
summary: Moropant Trimbak Pingle was the Peshwa under Shivaji.

title: What was the Chauth?
description: What was Chauth in the Maratha revenue system?
hint: It represented one-fourth of assessed revenue.
summary: Chauth was a levy generally equal to one-fourth of revenue.

title: What was Sardeshmukhi?
description: What was Sardeshmukhi in the Maratha revenue system?
hint: It was traditionally associated with an additional ten percent levy.
summary: Sardeshmukhi was an additional levy generally amounting to 10 percent.

title: Who succeeded Shivaji?
description: Who succeeded Shivaji Maharaj after his death in 1680?
hint: He was Shivaji's elder son.
summary: Sambhaji succeeded Shivaji as ruler of the Maratha kingdom.

title: Who captured Sambhaji in 1689?
description: Sambhaji was captured during the Mughal-Maratha conflict under which Mughal emperor?
hint: He was the Mughal emperor who spent much of his later reign in the Deccan.
summary: Sambhaji was captured and executed during Aurangzeb's reign in 1689.

title: Who succeeded Sambhaji?
description: Who became the Maratha ruler after Sambhaji's death?
hint: He was Shivaji's younger son.
summary: Rajaram succeeded Sambhaji as the Maratha ruler.

title: Who led the Maratha resistance after Rajaram's death?
description: Who played a major leadership role in continuing resistance against the Mughals after Rajaram's death?
hint: She was Rajaram's widow.
summary: Tarabai led the Maratha resistance after Rajaram's death.

title: Who became Chhatrapati after the Mughal release of Shahu?
description: Which Maratha ruler emerged as the principal claimant to the Maratha throne after his release from Mughal captivity?
hint: He was the son of Sambhaji.
summary: Shahu I became the principal Chhatrapati after his release.

title: Who became Peshwa under Shahu I in 1713?
description: Who was appointed Peshwa by Shahu I in 1713 and established the office as a major political institution?
hint: He belonged to the Bhat family.
summary: Balaji Vishwanath became Peshwa in 1713.

title: Who succeeded Balaji Vishwanath as Peshwa?
description: Who became Peshwa after the death of Balaji Vishwanath in 1720?
hint: He was known for his military campaigns and expansion.
summary: Bajirao I succeeded Balaji Vishwanath as Peshwa.

title: Which Peshwa is famous for defeating the Nizam at Palkhed?
description: Who defeated the Nizam of Hyderabad at the Battle of Palkhed in 1728?
hint: He was the second Peshwa of the Bhat family.
summary: Bajirao I defeated the Nizam at Palkhed in 1728.

title: Which battle demonstrated Bajirao I's military skill against the Nizam?
description: Which 1728 battle ended with a Maratha victory over the Nizam?
hint: The battle took place in the present-day Nashik region.
summary: The Battle of Palkhed was a major victory of Bajirao I over the Nizam.

title: Who was the Maratha Peshwa during the Battle of Bhopal?
description: Which Peshwa secured a major victory over the Nizam's forces near Bhopal in 1738?
hint: He was known as a highly successful Maratha military commander.
summary: Bajirao I led the Marathas in the campaign resulting in the Treaty of Bhopal in 1738.

title: Which city became the principal seat of the Peshwas?
description: Which city developed into the political center of the Peshwa-led Maratha state?
hint: It is a major city in present-day Maharashtra.
summary: Pune became the principal seat of the Peshwas.

title: Who succeeded Bajirao I as Peshwa?
description: Who became Peshwa after Bajirao I's death in 1740?
hint: He was Bajirao I's son.
summary: Balaji Baji Rao, also known as Nana Saheb, succeeded Bajirao I.

title: Who was the Maratha Peshwa at the Third Battle of Panipat?
description: Who was the Peshwa when the Marathas fought Ahmad Shah Abdali in 1761?
hint: He was also known as Nana Saheb.
summary: Balaji Baji Rao was the Peshwa during the Third Battle of Panipat.

title: Who led the Maratha army at the Third Battle of Panipat?
description: Who served as the principal commander of the Maratha army at the Third Battle of Panipat?
hint: He was the cousin of Peshwa Balaji Baji Rao.
summary: Sadashivrao Bhau led the main Maratha army at Panipat.

title: Who defeated the Marathas at the Third Battle of Panipat?
description: Who commanded the Afghan forces that defeated the Marathas in 1761?
hint: He was the Afghan ruler also known as Ahmad Shah Durrani.
summary: Ahmad Shah Abdali defeated the Marathas at Panipat in 1761.

title: In which year was the Third Battle of Panipat fought?
description: Identify the year of the Third Battle of Panipat between the Marathas and Ahmad Shah Abdali.
hint: It was fought in the 18th century.
summary: The Third Battle of Panipat was fought in 1761.

title: Who became Peshwa after Panipat?
description: Who became Peshwa in 1761 after the death of Balaji Baji Rao?
hint: He is often regarded as one of the later capable Peshwas.
summary: Madhavrao I became Peshwa in 1761.

title: Who was Mahadji Scindia?
description: Mahadji Scindia was a major Maratha leader associated with which house?
hint: The family was based in Gwalior.
summary: Mahadji Scindia was the leading figure of the Scindia house of Gwalior.

title: Which Maratha house was associated with Indore?
description: Which prominent Maratha ruling house established its power around Indore?
hint: Malhar Rao was the founder of this prominent house.
summary: The Holkar house was associated with Indore.

title: Which Maratha house ruled from Baroda?
description: Which Maratha ruling family became prominent in Baroda?
hint: The family established itself in Gujarat.
summary: The Gaekwad house was associated with Baroda.

title: Which Maratha house ruled from Nagpur?
description: Which Maratha ruling family established its center at Nagpur?
hint: The family was a branch of the Bhonsle dynasty.
summary: The Bhonsle house of Nagpur was a major Maratha power.

title: Who founded the Holkar dynasty's prominence?
description: Who established the foundations of the Holkar family's power in the Maratha confederacy?
hint: He served under Bajirao I.
summary: Malhar Rao Holkar established the foundations of Holkar power.

title: Who was Ahilyabai Holkar?
description: Ahilyabai Holkar was the celebrated ruler of which Maratha state?
hint: Her capital was Maheshwar.
summary: Ahilyabai Holkar was the renowned ruler of the Holkar state.

title: Who was Nana Phadnavis?
description: Nana Phadnavis was an influential statesman of the Maratha confederacy during which period?
hint: He was particularly influential after the death of Madhavrao I.
summary: Nana Phadnavis was a prominent statesman and diplomat of the later Maratha confederacy.

title: Which Anglo-Maratha War ended with the Treaty of Salbai?
description: The Treaty of Salbai in 1782 brought which Anglo-Maratha conflict to an end?
hint: It was the first major war between the British East India Company and the Marathas.
summary: The First Anglo-Maratha War ended with the Treaty of Salbai.

title: Which treaty brought the Peshwa under British protection in 1802?
description: Which treaty did Peshwa Baji Rao II sign with the British East India Company?
hint: The treaty was signed at Bassein.
summary: The Treaty of Bassein was signed in 1802 between Baji Rao II and the British.

title: Which Anglo-Maratha War ended the Peshwa's political power?
description: Which war resulted in the defeat of the Marathas and the end of the Peshwa's political authority?
hint: It was fought from 1817 to 1818.
summary: The Third Anglo-Maratha War ended the Peshwa's political power in 1818.
